title: fix(worktrees): resume repository repair after bounded passes
body:
Related: #182204, #165858

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated five-minute repository-repair timeouts that prevent later linked worktree indexes from receiving missing objects during `openclaw worktrees gc --retry-deferred`.

## User Impact

Explicit retries make progress across checkouts, including after a Gateway restart, while preserving staged and working files. The five-minute repair budget, 4,096-object limit, two-child admission limit, low-priority Git, and explicit-only fetch policy remain. A single checkout whose own inventory exceeds the entire budget can still require repository repair; the cursor lets other checkouts proceed rather than declaring that checkout healthy. Nested-repository removal protection remains unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pack consolidation was already incremental in #182204; object repair still inventoried every linked index before its first fetch. Repair now inventories one checkout at a time and records the last attempted checkout in the existing machine-state database. That scheduling position survives interruption and is cleared after a complete sweep. It is never a health receipt or removal authorization. Healthy object IDs no longer fill the inventory output.

Maintenance also acquires a content slot before the ref queue, matching content writers. The reverse order could hold the ref queue while waiting for both slots occupied by writers waiting on that queue.

Runtime production code grows by 22 lines to retain the durable scheduling position and replace the global inventory loop. Benchmark/harness code grows by 89 lines; tests by 165 lines. The requested non-test/non-doc diff therefore totals +111 lines, including measurement tooling. There is no new schema, configuration option, cache, or alternate repair path.

## Evidence

Both new regressions fail on the original owner: repeated budget exhaustion starves a later staged missing blob after reopening state, and maintenance deadlocks with active ref writers. With the fix, the changed and directly related test files pass: 39 tests, with one Linux-only test skipped on macOS. The restart test checks exact index bytes and unstaged content. Changed-file lint, format, and whitespace checks pass. Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable) found no actionable P0–P2 findings.

The synthetic repository contains 1,536 packs, including 1,257 promisor packs, and 1,536 distinct 32 KiB blobs (48 MiB). Three fresh-owner candidate passes reduce packs **1,536 → 236 → 4 → 4**, taking **215.79 s, 27.21 s, 0.22 s**; every pass fits the five-minute bound. Baseline already converges **1,536 → 236 → 4 → 4** in **191.20 s, 44.07 s, 0.35 s**. These shared-host timings establish bounded completion, not a calibrated speedup. All blob identities/sizes and `git fsck --full --no-dangling` pass on both sides.

An abort immediately after verified replacement publication leaves all 236 original packs intact. A restarted owner reduces that interrupted 238-pack layout to **2 → 2 → 2** in **23.89 s, 0.10 s, 0.13 s**, with all 1,536 blobs verified and full Git integrity clean.

The per-script header documents the reproducible pack workload; the shared performance README is unchanged. No live repositories or production Gateways were modified or load-tested.

The required canonical Gateway campaign exposed a harness defect: its post-round drain required all subscriber traffic to stop while its own background metadata and cron workload remained active. The accompanying harness fix scopes the quiet window to tracked foreground and committed-injection receipts. Active streams, pending injections, exact delivery, foreground parity, and sequence checks remain enforced. Its 17 focused tests and changed-file lint/format pass, and independent supplemental review is clean.

The canonical campaign completed all eight ten-minute arms: timing AB/BA and separate allocation AB/BA, with 10,800 sessions, 65 clients, 40 enabled plugins, four concurrent tool-using mock turns per round, native subagents, and list/search/history/startup/diff/reconnect churn. Each arm completed 40 primary turns and 40 primary tool calls; all eight plugin inventories matched, and the harness accepted RPC, connection, sequence, foreground parity, and exactly-once injection checks. Normal maintenance stayed enabled. This standard workload does not invoke explicit deferred object repair; the real-Git owner proofs above cover that behavior.

Both built revisions use source `2810b07ba0e7`, with the candidate applying this PR's maintenance patch. Runtime inputs and tooling remained fixed through the campaign. The runtime builds completed successfully. Build metadata was captured before committing the patch, so the separately verified entry hashes distinguish the artifacts: base `07264fad4488d40c8a283a13ab3017279a614cf1baf8461cb9f135d18a0417eb`, candidate `5a2a877227509d7dd96a4bbe50e98ca80aea647f45bb0bf3077a07dbb7a02bf5`.

This is a resumability/deadlock repair, not a claimed general Gateway speedup. CPU and allocation increases are reported rather than hidden; neither crosses the declared CPU/allocation rejection rule: a mean signed paired increase of at least 20%, or at least 10% in both pairs. The aggregate percentage uses the absolute paired mean divided by mean baseline cost. GC and end-of-window memory decreased. Client and handler latency tails need the predeclared A/A controls below before attribution.

The initial checkout-versus-runtime-snapshot campaign was excluded for a verified setup asymmetry: the source checkout discovered two additional disabled QA manifests. Its one completed pair observed CPU 8.751/10.499%, GC 0.170/0.441 s/min, loop p99 33.047/51.085 ms, and list p99 127.676/291.315 ms (base/candidate). Those values are not attributed to the patch. Matching runtime snapshots removed the discovery difference; their full-size inventories match exactly. An earlier setup smoke also caught the receipt-drain defect fixed here.

Two predeclared ten-minute A/A timing pairs (40 additional measured minutes) completed on byte-identical baseline runtime snapshots in separate matching paths, using the same workload, clock anchor, and instrumentation. All four control inventories match the comparison inventory, and all control correctness checks pass.

| A/A pair | Client list p99 A / B (ms) | Signed B−A | Handler interpolated p99 A / B (ms) | Signed B−A |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 135.50 / 97.60 | -37.90 ms (-28.0%) | 106.75 / 81.35 | -25.40 ms (-23.8%) |
| 2 | 52.75 / 73.50 | +20.74 ms (+39.3%) | 44.09 / 68.47 | +24.38 ms (+55.3%) |

Identical-source latency differences reverse sign and exceed 20% in magnitude. This does not prove the A/B latency increase harmless; it makes attribution inconclusive on this shared-host protocol. No latency improvement or confirmed latency regression is claimed. The change is justified by the reproduced resumability/deadlock defects and their passing regression/progress proofs, with the measured CPU/allocation tradeoffs above.

The reviewed commits rebased cleanly onto `54408a978fc9`; `git range-diff` confirms both patches are unchanged. Exact-head [CI run 40299784559, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40299784559) completed on `24c6a067b527efdf3282ac82e51ee099347a468d`. Typechecks, lint, changed-boundary checks, security checks, and all other test jobs passed. The only failed test job is `checks-node-changed-compact-large-8` ([job 121495324440](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40299784559/job/121495324440)); the aggregate CI gate is red because of it.

The failure is inherited: `src/gateway/server.required-worker-profile.test.ts:582`, case `required workspace commit fences runtime authority after preparation`, expects `Session changed during worker admission` but receives `SQLite session state changed while preparing session-entry.patch`. Running `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server.required-worker-profile.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` separately on the exact PR head and unchanged baseline `54408a978fc9` reproduces that identical assertion, with 1 failed and 16 passed on each. The test file is unchanged by this PR. This records failed CI accurately and qualifies the scoped inherited-failure landing exception; no CI rerun or unrelated repair is included.
